content:
The correct phrase is **"eke out"** (not "eek out").

"To eke out" means to:
- Make something last longer by using it sparingly
- Barely manage to make a living or survive
- Supplement or add to something inadequate

Examples:
- "They had to eke out their food supplies during the winter"
- "She eked out a living as a freelance writer"

"Eek" is just an exclamation of fear or surprise (like when you see a mouse!), so "eek out" would be incorrect.
